scenes.text: Machines can learn in three very different ways, a bit like how children learn. [1] With a teacher, by exploring on their own, or by trial and error. [2] Let's understand supervised, unsupervised, and reinforcement learning.

Here are the three types. [1] Supervised learning, learning from labelled examples, like a teacher giving you the answers. [2] Unsupervised learning, finding patterns in data with no labels at all. [3] And reinforcement learning, learning by trial and error, with rewards and penalties.

Supervised learning is the most common. [1] You show the model thousands of examples, each with the correct answer, called a label. [2] Like emails marked spam or not spam, [3] photos labelled cat or dog, [4] or house details with their prices.

data.definition: Learning from examples that come with the correct answer, called labels.

scenes.text: Unsupervised learning has no answers at all. [1] The model just looks for natural groups in the data. Here, shoppers group themselves by what they buy. [2] Now a new shopper arrives, [3] and lands near the fitness group, so the store can suggest sports gear.

Reinforcement learning is learning by trial and error. [1] An agent tries an action, sees what happens, and gets a reward or a penalty. Take a game playing AI. [2] It moves, and loses points for crashing. [3] It gains points for collecting coins. [4] It tries new paths, and scores big. [5] And after millions of games, it becomes an expert.

Here's a quick cheat sheet. [1] Three types, side by side. [2] Supervised needs labels, like a spam filter. [3] Unsupervised needs no labels, like finding customer groups. [4] And reinforcement uses rewards instead of labels, like a game playing AI.

Here's a common myth. [1] People think modern AI uses only one of these. [2] Big models like ChatGPT use all three. Pre-training learns patterns from raw text, fine-tuning uses labelled examples, and human feedback uses rewards, which we'll explore in a later episode.

data.myth: Modern AI uses only one type of learning.
data.fact: Big models use all three: raw-text pre-training, labelled fine-tuning, and reward-based feedback.
